pageCache.pageTitle: Bromley Trust Alternative Provision Academy - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Bromley Trust Academy
As a school, we believe that we ‘decide’ our own futures
Discovery
Every day we try to discover new things
Endeavour
Community
Believing in our Communities and being leaders there
Independence
Become independent pupils
Decisions
Making sensible decisions
Everyday
Doing all of these everyday
Welcome fromRob Freeman - Headteacher Emily Richards - Head of School Gina Queeley - Head of School
At Bromley Trust Academy, we believe in the potential of every young person. Across our three campuses – we provide a supportive and high-quality education tailored to each pupil’s needs. Our dedicated staff work closely with pupils and their families to identify need, help them re-engage with learning, overcome barriers and achieve success.
At our Midfield Campus, we provide primary-aged children with a stimulating learning environment, building confidence and independence. Preparing them for their next steps - whether this is into a specialist provision or a return to mainstream school.
At our Hayes Campus, we work with 11–16-year-olds who have been permanently excluded (or are at risk of exclusion). We help pupils rebuild confidence and achieve industry-relevant qualifications to progress successfully into further education or an apprenticeship.
At our Blenheim Provision, we support pupils in Years 10–11 who are supported by CAMHS, providing a calm and nurturing environment where they can thrive academically and emotionally. Across all our campuses, we celebrate achievements and focus on preparing our pupils for life beyond school.
Our Vision & Values
We believe in securing the best for all our pupils, with inclusion and cohesion at the heart of our school's ethos. We aim to raise standards by supporting the development of every child as a reflective pupil, striving to ensure that everything we do has a positive impact on them.
We are proud of our record in promoting equality for all. We offer a happy, secure and stimulating learning environment in which the whole school community can grow in confidence and develop to their full potential.
As a school, we believe that we ‘decide’ our own futures

pageCache.pageTitle: Bromley Trust Alternative Provision Academy - SMSC and British Values
pageCache.text:
SMSC and British Values
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development
The Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC) development of our pupils is inherent in our curriculum, our behaviours and the culture of the school.
Bromley Trust Academy strives to develop pupils that are responsible and respectful with a strong moral purpose. SMSC supports this development so that our pupils become life-long learners, who play constructive roles as citizens in our diverse and multi-cultural society.
It is the responsibility of all staff at Bromley Trust Academy to ensure SMSC development takes place in all lessons and around the school at all times.
SMSC has four different aspects, formulated to help our pupils grow into responsible members of the community.
We encourage Bromley Trust Academy pupils to display the following traits:
Promoting British Values
Bromley Trust Academy is committed to serving its community. It recognises the multi-cultural, multi faith and ever-changing nature of the Britain. It also understands the vital role it has in ensuring that groups or individuals within the school are not subjected to intimidation or radicalisation by those wishing to unduly, or illegally, influence them.
We follow equal opportunities guidance which guarantees that there will be no discrimination against any individual or group, regardless of faith, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, political or financial status, or similar. Bromley Trust Academy is dedicated to preparing students for their adult life beyond the formal examined curriculum and ensuring that it promotes and reinforces British values to all its pupils.
The Government emphasises that schools are required to ensure that key ‘British Values’ are taught in all UK schools. The five British Values are:
The examples that follow show some of the many ways Bromley Trust Academy seeks to embed British values.
The principle of democracy is consistently being reinforced at Bromley Trust Academy, with democracy processes being used for important decisions within the school community. For example, School Council decisions and ideas as well as students and parents providing valuable input into school/ trust policies.
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced at Bromley Trust Academy. Pupils are taught the rules and expectations of the school which are highlighted in our Behaviour Policy. Pupils are taught the value and the reasons behind laws that govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service reinforce this message.
At Bromley Trust Academy, pupils are actively encouraged to make independent choices, with the knowledge that they are in a safe, secure and supportive environment. Staff at Bromley Trust Academy educate and provide boundaries for pupils to make informed choices, through a safe environment and an empowering education.
Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised on how to exercise these safely, for example through e-safety and PSHE.
Bromley Trust Academy has a robust anti-bullying culture and has in place a comprehensive Behaviour Policy.
Respect is a strong part of Bromley Trust Academy and is part of its core values. Pupils learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect and this is reiterated through its teaching and learning environments.
Tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs
This is achieved through equipping pupils with the ability to understand their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving the opportunities to experience such diversity within the school community.
Bromley Trust Academy strives endlessly to ensure that its pupils leave with the strongest foundation of values upon which to build a successful life and a successful contribution to our society.

Head's Welcome
Welcome to the Midfield Campus of Bromley Trust Academy, part of London South East Academies Trust.
As a school we aim to broaden horizons for our pupils, supporting them until they are ready to transition into their next school. We work hard to ensure that every young person we work with receives the best possible learning opportunities.
The happiness and success of every child is central to our school’s work and promoting high levels of achievement is key. We are recognised as a 'Good' school by Ofsted (September 2023- click here for the full report).
Our Midfield Campus provides education and support for 5 -11 year olds pupils who are at risk of being, or have been, permanently excluded from primary school. We aim to work with these young people to identify and remove barriers to learning, so that where possible they can return to a mainstream school or access a specialist school setting if more appropriate.
We pride ourselves on inclusion across the school - and we expect high standards. Children attend in smart uniform, participate in challenging lessons and come together regularly in assemblies and celebrations. We focus on preparing our pupils for life beyond our doors.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bromley Trust Alternative Provision Academy - Careers Guidance
pageCache.text:
Careers Guidance
Careers Guidance
Through a planned Careers programme, Bromley Trust Academy Blenheim aims to contribute to raising aspirations, creating positive self-image, increasing self-confidence, improving motivation and overcoming barriers to success. Our school has a critical role to play in preparing our young people for the next stage of their education or training and beyond. Our expectations are high, so every student is challenged appropriately and acquires the knowledge, skills and attitudes for lifelong learning that employers will value. This will help every young person to enhance their employability and realise their potential.
Our Careers leader is Michelle Graydon.
Email: michelle.graydon@bromleybeaconacademy.org.uk
Careers Skills
We recognise the importance of developing the careers skills of our young people through our provision for Careers Guidance. We believe that young people need these skills to manage their own careers and to contribute to the well-being of themselves, their families, the communities and the wider society of which they are a part, the environment and the economy.The school's careers provision, therefore, needs to help students to develop their self-efficacy, raise their aspirations and help them carry out career exploration. They must also become more adaptable and resilient, make decisions and transitions, be more enterprising and be able to present themselves well in applications and interviews.We are therefore working towards the 8 Gatsby Principles to ensure all our young people are able to access high quality information, advice and guidance throughout their time with us.The eight Gatsby benchmarks of Good Career Guidance:
As part of our careers programme we believe employability skills are extremely important, which is why we ensure all young people have work experience opportunities in KS4.
We also believe ‘employability and transferable skills’ are an essential part of our day to day curriculum to give our young people the skills to make them ‘employable’ in the future. The top 10 skills that employers want and seek in potential employees are:
A stable careers programme
Learning from career and labour market information
Addressing the needs of each pupil
Linking curriculum learning to careers
Encounters with employers and employees
Experiences of workplaces
Encounters with further and higher education
Personal guidance
Communication and interpersonal skills
Problem solving skills
Using your initiative and being self-motivated
Organisational skills
Working under pressure and to deadlines
Team working
Ability to learn and adapt
Numeracy
Valuing diversity and difference
Negotiation Skills
Careers Programme
There is a planned Careers Programme throughout the year for all students from Year 7. The programme is reviewed regularly to ensure the needs of all students are being met.
Monitoring, review and development of CEIAG
The school has been assessed and accredited as “making good progress towards meeting all the accreditation criteria incorporating the Gatsby Benchmarks”
The Careers programme is monitored through the Careers Development plan, which is linked to the School Development plan.
All careers events are evaluated by staff, students and providers to ensure learning objectives are met.
Destinations at KS4 are closely monitored and students are supported after leaving school where necessary.
The number of NEET (Not in Employment, Education or Training) figures remain low and preferably at 0%

Careers Next Steps for Year 11 Pupils
Careers - Next Steps for Year 11 Pupils
Pupils and Parents came together today for a meeting about the next steps in the Post 16 journey.
First the Pupils heard from the Careers Leader and Careers Adviser, who reminded them about all the careers activities they have already competed and what’s coming up next in the process. Then Alison Oothuizan, the Director of Additional Learning Support and Karyn Thomas, the Assistant Director of Additional Learning Support spoke about the enrolment process and support available to pupils at Bromley college.
This was followed by Jemal Gray, Head of Behaviour (LSEC) who outlined the expectations of pupils, both in class and around the campus. Pupils and parents then had the opportunity to ask questions.
This is part of our commitment to pupils and parents as part of our Careers Programme to provide information in an accessible way.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bromley Trust Alternative Provision Academy - Careers education at BTA Hayes
pageCache.text:
Careers education at BTA Hayes
Careers education at BTA Hayes
At Bromley Trust Academy Hayes, we are committed to ensuring that our inclusive careers programme supports all our pupils to develop their potential and raise their career aspirations. Our aim is for every pupil to feel confident about having conversations about careers and their next steps after leaving school.
To support our Year 11 pupils as they make key progression decisions, we invite parents and carers into school to speak with representatives from colleges and training providers, ask questions, and explore the different pathways available to their children. This is followed up with a second parent and student meeting to provide an understanding of the support available and expectations of colleges.
London South East Colleges (LSEC) sits in the same education group (Elevare Civic Education Group) as our Multi Academy Trust (London South East Academies Trust). Therefore, our school has a strong relationship with the college, with clear progression pathways available for our learners. I have the opportunity to organise VIP tours of LSEC’s Bromley campus, , enabling our pupils to walk around the college in small groups. They get to ask questions about the different pathways available and to experience the college environment during a normal working day.
In addition, I have taken our Year 11 students to an apprenticeship event at LSEC’s Orpington campus. This was a great opportunity for them to take part in interactive activities and learn more about how apprenticeships work.
All Year 11 pupils receive one-to-one interviews with our independent careers adviser, Michelle Graydon. During these sessions, Michelle supports pupils with their next steps and helps them complete their college application forms.
Michelle also supports our Year 11 pupils when they attend their Subject Information Meetings at LSEC Bromley. This helps them feel more confident and supported during the transition process.
Our December Academic Review Day provides the opportunity for us to hold a mini transitions and Careers Fair. All our pupils, along with their parents/carers are encouraged to chat with local colleges, employers and support agencies as part of their visit to the school.
Apprenticeship Week and National Careers Week earlier this term were also enjoyed by all our pupils. Posters were displayed around the school to inspire them and raise awareness about apprenticeships. During tutor time, pupils took part in activities that encouraged discussion and helped start some really positive conversations about careers and apprenticeship pathways.
These activities have particularly inspired our Key Stage 3 pupils, many of whom have shown a strong interest in learning more about apprenticeships and the opportunities available to them.
Our inclusive Careers Programme also offers so much more, with industry visits, work experience, an annual in-school careers fair and strengths & skills sessions for the younger students, there is something for everybody and opportunities for everyone to aspire to!

pageCache.text:
Therapeutic Wellbeing
Therapeutic Wellbeing
We are committed to ensuring the wellbeing of all of our pupils. Health and wellbeing programmes in schools lead to significant improvements in children's mental health, academic success and social and emotional skills.
Therapy and Wellbeing
At BTA Midfield, we recognise that children need to feel safe, understood and supported in order to thrive and reach their full potential.
Supporting children’s social, emotional and mental health (SEMH) is an important part of school life. We recognise that wellbeing is closely connected to learning, relationships, communication and a child’s ability to engage positively with school.
Our Therapy and Wellbeing Service provides additional therapeutic support for children who may benefit from having dedicated time and space to explore their feelings, develop their emotional wellbeing and build positive relationships.
Our therapeutic provision works alongside the wider support offered by the school, including the work of teachers, support staff and other professionals. We take a child-centred approach, recognising that every child is different and may communicate and express themselves in different ways.
We are fortunate to have a HCPC-registered Music Therapist as part of our school community. Our therapist leads the therapeutic provision and works closely with school staff to identify children who may benefit from individual or group therapeutic support.
The therapist uses their professional knowledge and experience to help each child find ways of engaging that feel safe, accessible and meaningful to them. This may involve music, play, creativity, conversation and other interactive activities.
Therapy can provide children with an opportunity to express feelings and experiences, develop their communication and emotional regulation skills, strengthen relationships and explore difficult experiences at their own pace.
Children who are identified as likely to benefit from ongoing therapeutic support may be offered weekly individual or group therapy sessions. The therapy caseload is reviewed regularly to ensure that support continues to reflect the needs of the children and the wider school community.
Alongside regular therapy, children who are not currently receiving weekly sessions can access occasional wellbeing drop-in sessions. These may be requested by a member of staff or, where appropriate, by the child themselves.
Drop-in sessions provide a safe, supportive space for a child who may be having a particularly difficult day, needs some time to regulate, or would benefit from expressing themselves through conversation, music or creative activity.
Therapy and wellbeing support is provided in a safe, supportive and non-judgemental environment. Information shared in sessions is treated respectfully and confidentially within the therapist's professional and safeguarding responsibilities.
For more information about our Therapy and Wellbeing Service, please contact our therapist, Kate Brooks: kate.brooks@bromleytrust.lseat.org.uk
What is Music Therapy?
Music Therapy is a form of therapy that uses music and creative interaction to support a child’s emotional wellbeing, communication, relationships and development.
Music can offer children a different way to communicate and express themselves, particularly when finding the right words feels difficult. No previous musical experience or ability is needed.
In sessions, the therapist may use instruments, singing, rhythm, improvisation, songwriting, movement, play and other creative activities. Sessions can include both structured activities and child-led exploration, depending on what is most appropriate for the individual child.

Every child is different, so the therapist adapts sessions to the child’s individual needs, interests and stage of development. Sessions are supportive, non-judgemental and take place in a safe space where children can explore and express themselves at their own pace.

Therapeutic Wellbeing
Therapeutic Wellbeing
At BTA we are fully committed to supporting our staff and students in their mental health wellbeing. We prioritise social emotional and mental health (SEMH) within every aspect of school life - policies & environment, curriculum, special events & campaigns - to positively impact outcomes for students. This support in school can lead to significant improvements in young people's mental health, academic success and social and emotional skills.
In recognising that people need support to thrive and reach their full potential, we have a Counsellor, Mental Health and Wellbeing lead, a number of mental health first aiders and all staff accessing regular training in order to support our students with their SEMH needs.
For Students
Therapeutic work is tailored according to needs, offering a holistic approach to support emotional and psychological wellbeing. The aim of therapy may include improving self-awareness, self-esteem, relationships, building confidence, coping strategies, anger management, general wellbeing or making difficult events and emotions more bearable. These interventions may occur individually or in groups.
All students are invited to a 30-minute taster session when they join us; this gives them the opportunity to meet our onsite therapist, see the therapeutic space and get a sense of what therapy is like at our school. During the session, they are able to begin building a positive and trusting relationship and gain an understanding of confidentiality and its limits within therapy.
Following the taster sessions, students will be made aware of the therapy offered here. They can be referred for regular therapy by themselves, parents, staff or agencies. This consists of them accessing counselling on a weekly basis, which is reviewed at the end of each half-term. There is often a waiting list for this service.
We work as a team to change any stigma that a student may have against a therapeutic intervention by building a positive and trusting relationship from when they start. The therapist continues to be a presence around the school throughout the day so the students have the opportunity to approach them if they feel they need to. Some students find that a commitment to long-term weekly therapy is too much, others may have had previous negative experiences of counselling or don’t believe it will be beneficial for them. These views are valid and important; no student will be forced to participate. For therapy to take place, there must be psychological contact, and this does not occur if a student is not invested.
All students have the opportunity to access drop-in and crisis sessions throughout the week as and when needed. The therapist endeavours to check-in with all students throughout the week and works with the wider staff team to identity students in need of further support. Students are also able to ask for a drop-in session and this will be accommodated around timetable sessions.
For Parents and Carers
The onsite therapy team is here to support you and happy to hear from any of our parents/carers. We believe it is fundamental to set up open channels of communication with all of the adults who feature in the lives of our students. Our ethos at Bromley Trust Academy is to adopt a ‘whole school’ approach to mental health and wellbeing and give them the opportunity to thrive in a supportive learning environment.
Carnegie Centre of Excellence for Mental Health in Schools Award:
Bromley Trust Academy are working towards excellence in mental health practice. We are looking to have this recognised and developed with a national award level. We are continually working to improve and strengthen the mental health of students, parents and staff. We believe the award will reflect our commitment to our school structures, environment, and ethos, which supports positive mental health and wellbeing. Achieving this award will be a whole school effort and will take into account students, parents and governor's voice.
